newsitem.title: USA: Felcor buys 50 percent stake in 8 hotels.
newsitem.headline: Felcor buys 50 percent stake in 8 hotels.

text.p: FelCor Suite Hotels Inc. Monday said it will pay about $100 million for interests of about 50 percent in eight Embassy Suites hotels from affiliates of a General Electric Co. unit and Promus Hotel Corp.

Felcor, the nation's largest owner of Embassy Suites hotels, also said it has signed a letter of intent to pay $39 million for full ownership of two other hotels from the affiliates of the General Electric Pension Trust and Promus.
The $100 million for the stake in the eight Embassy Suites includes FelCor's $43 million share of existing debt, the Irving, Texas-based company said.

The cash portion of the purchase price for these 10 hotels, together with the cost of limited renovations, is expected to come from the net proceeds of FelCor's offering of 3 million shares of common stock, as announced on Friday.
Promus will retain a 50 percent stake in the eight joint venture hotels, and manage them.
Felcor said it will convert the two wholly-owned hotels to the Doubletree Guest Suites brand within 90 days after the deal closes. They will be managed by a Doubletree Hotels Corp. affiliate.
FelCor was formed in July 1994 by Chairman Hervey Feldman, the founding President of Embassy Suites, and long-time hotel and restaurant executive Thomas Corcoran, Jr.
FelCor's stock rose 50 cents to $35.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
